office_does: A Lewis County PUD commissioner sits on the three-member elected board that sets policy and rates for the public electric utility serving about 35,000 customers outside Centralia, for a six-year term.
race_blurb: Open seat: appointed Commissioner Dave Muller, named in 2025 after Michael Kelly's seat was vacated, is not on the ballot, and every PUD voter elects the District 1 commissioner for the short and full terms. Retired PUD engineer Steve Grega stresses low rates and Cowlitz Falls Dam relicensing. Technology architect and former PUD employee Jeff Baine stresses transparency, broadband and reliable, affordable power.

candidates.summary: Retired Lewis County PUD engineer of 37 years and former Army Corps of Engineers engineer, running on low rates, reliability and Cowlitz Falls Dam relicensing.
highlights: Worked on licensing, construction and operation of Cowlitz Falls Dam during his PUD career [S1]
Says rising power costs and state renewable mandates mean every other expense must be closely checked to keep rates low [S1]
Would plan Cowlitz Falls relicensing now and minimize its costs [S1]

candidates.summary: Lifelong Lewis County resident and Barracuda Networks solutions architect, a former PUD employee and Broadband Action Committee president, running on transparency and reliable, affordable power.
highlights: Former long-time PUD employee and former president of the Lewis County Broadband Action Committee [S2]
Wants PUD decisions made with transparency and ratepayers at the center [S1]
Prioritizes broadband expansion, infrastructure investment and affordable power while meeting the Clean Energy Transformation Act [S1]
